chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) performed ablution (wudu), so he washed his face and his forearms, then he wiped upon his head and upon his slipper (open from the front), and did not enter his hand beneath the straps.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) perform ablution with respect to wiping over his footwear?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir, establishes the permissibility of wiping over leather slippers (khuff) during ablution, a practice attributed directly to Imam Ali. It serves as a foundational proof in Shia jurisprudence for the validity of partial wiping rather than full washing of the feet when wearing khuff, emphasizing the practical ease granted to the faithful. The specific detail of not inserting the hand under the strap confirms the integrity of the covering during the wiping action.
